title: Vivaldi’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

entries.speaker: User
entries.text:
[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — Vivaldi’s Missing Symphony (work id vivaldi-symphony-1)

Vivaldi is the one Baroque composer in this batch who did write pieces called sinfonia: short three-movement works for strings and continuo, fast–slow–fast, related to the Italian opera overture. This is a new one in that form, in G minor, with one liberty: a solo violin from his concertos, which leads the first violins in the tuttis and has episodes of its own. No theme is taken from Vivaldi.

Instrumentation (7 staves): solo violin, violins I and II, violas, cellos, double basses, harpsichord. In the slow movement the orchestral strings play pizzicato.

Movements
I. Allegro, G minor, 4/4: ritornello form. The ritornello has three parts: a hammering theme for all the strings in octaves, a falling-fifths sequence in sixteenth notes, and a cadence. It returns in B flat and D minor; four solo episodes come between.
II. Largo, E flat major, 3/4: the solo violin sings over plucked strings; first part repeated.
III. Presto, G minor, 3/8: a driving dance in two repeated halves on one eight-bar theme.

Length: about seven minutes, the scale of Vivaldi’s own sinfonias. Stylistic approach: short motifs, sequences on the circle of fifths, unison tuttis, terraced dynamics, idiomatic broken-chord figuration. Compromise known from the start: themes, the slow movement’s melody and the chord of every beat are written by hand; the broken-chord figuration of the solo episodes and sequences, the inner parts, basses and harpsichord are realised by a program from the chord plan, which suits this style better than most.

entries.text:
Published live draft revision 1 with this public change note:
First draft of all three movements: the G minor Allegro with its unison ritornello and solo-violin episodes, the Largo for solo violin over plucked strings, and the Presto in 3/8. A revision pass follows.
